title: Signs of Trump and GOP panic grow ahead of the midterms | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

Republicans have hadreason to worry about the 2026 midterm electionsfor a while now.

But there are growing signs that their fears are spilling over into panic — and that the GOP, including President Donald Trump, senses things could get really bad.

That doesn’t mean thingswillturn out that way. And there are plenty of examples of parties overzealously slamming the panic button late in the campaign.

But the Trump-era GOP has generally been a rather sanguine political party, and what we’ve seen in recent days and weeks is anything but.

Trump has insisted Republicans will do well and that the many polls suggesting otherwise are wrong. But his actions increasingly point in a different direction:

The GOP was already playing defense in five states Trump won by between 11 and 16 points, with the most recent addition being Kansas — a state Trump won by 16 points two years ago and that hasn’t elected a Democratic senatorsince 1932.

But adding Nebraska and especially South Carolina to the mix is particularly striking.

And in case you thought Trump’s comments about South Carolina weren’t strategic, the GOP is sending $5 million to the Palmetto State to shore up Graham. Trump allies have also told CNN they are worried about the senator’s polling.

One of the most telling signs of broader GOP panic? Republicans feeling compelled todistance themselves from Trump even in these red areas— whether calling for an end to the Iran war, overhauling their websites to erase mentions of the president, or declining to campaign with Trump.

On Monday, the Houston Chronicle reported that Texas Gov. Greg Abbottwon’t appear with Trumpwhen the president visits San Antonio this week. Abbott’s campaign blamed scheduling conflicts, but these are the kinds of events GOP candidates would never have missed once upon a time, especially in a red state.

And indeed, many of the worst signs for the GOP are emanating from Texas.

There’s theawkward adfrom Senate nominee Ken Paxton’s estranged wife (who has accused him of infidelity) in which she encourages people to vote Republican. There arethe leakedaudio clipsin which Paxton is heard complaining about Trump and the national GOP hurting his campaign. And on Monday, GOP state Rep. Briscoe Cain posted on X: “If the election were held tomorrow, all state wide races go blue.”

Just to underscore how stunning that would be, Democrats haven’t wonanystatewide race in Texas since 1994. And this isn’t some moderate Republican spouting off; this is a MAGA lawmaker whotried to help overturnthe results of the 2020 election for Trump.

None of this means the GOP is doomed. While there are enough signs in the polling to cause the party to worry,Democrats’ path to the Senate majoritystill goes through those double-digit Trump states. That’s a high bar to clear.

And, we’ve seen before how parties can spend late money in lower-tier races that don’t wind up being particularly close. Back in 2020, Democrats spent some real moneyin Kansas, and the GOP sent money tobolster South Carolina; Republicans wound up winning those states by 11 and 10 points, respectively. Even some Democrats arepretty circumspectabout their chances in South Carolina this year.

But the increased desperation ahead of November 3 means it could be a long four weeks for the GOP.
